messages:
maria_storage: heads up — us-west2 NVMe pool hitting sustained ~180k read+write IOPS for the last 8m. GPU attach queue jumped from ~120 -> 220 and attach latencies are at 900ms-1.3s. anyone else seeing similar spikes?

alex_ops: seeing it on dashboards. spike aligns with cleanupd run at 02:10 UTC. provisioning backlog correlates with IOPS surge. :eyes:

jun_sre: oncall alerted, paging now. can we throttle cleanupd or shift scrub window? this is blocking some GPU launches.

maria_storage: temporarily paused cleanupd on two highest-IO nodes (node-uw2-123, node-uw2-124). command used: `kubectl annotate node node-uw2-123 cleanupd=false` — paused on those for now.

rachael_infra: good call. thinking about cgroup/blkio weight adjustments for cleanup workers. we can push a short-term weight drop for background jobs. also can we route new GPU provisioning to us-east1 while we stabilize?

alex_ops: we can add blkio weight and reduce cleanup concurrency. short-term fallback routing to us-east1 sounds easiest to avoid customer impact. also check prefix-KV cache eviction — looks like hot models are thrashing reads.

jun_sre: routing change applied: `route-policy set prefer=us-east1 for tag=gpu-provision` — monitoring now. I've lowered scrub concurrency from 6 -> 2 across the pool.

maria_storage: logs show a couple of CRC read errors on node-uw2-124 around the spike. snippet:
```
[2025-03-12T02:12:03Z] nvme0: Read error sector 0x7f2a3: retry=3
[2025-03-12T02:12:05Z] nvme0: media error
```
Not a full device failure but wear concentrated on a small extent.

alex_ops: ok — those media errors explain retries and latency. let's avoid heavy writes to those extents. Can we evict temp/model cache shards from disk to reduce small-block churn?

rachael_infra: applying an emergency throttling change to cleanupd: reduce aggressive delete window from 5m -> 30s and set concurrency to 1 for now. Pushing PR and rolling out. ops-bot will post status.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started for infra/cleanupd throttling (PR #432).

jun_sre: iostat shows attach queue down to ~60 within 3m of the throttles. IOPS down to ~40k. No new CRC errors in last 2m. :thumbsup:

maria_storage: thanks. please schedule a wear-map pass tomorrow to reassign writes away from those hot extents and add an alert for nvme CRC rate > 0.01% (to avoid silent degradation).

alex_ops: agreed. medium-term idea: move model shard hot-cache to ram-backed ephemeral FS for hottest tiers to cut nvme writes. need doc + cost estimate (RAM vs NVMe).

rachael_infra: i'll add RFC to the backlog and slot for next infra sprint. for now, re-enable cleanupd after 20m with concurrency=1 and keep routing fallback active for 1h.

jun_sre: closing the incident tentatively — will reopen if CRC rate or attach latency returns. key metrics before->after: attach-latency 1.2s -> 0.35s, iops 180k -> 42k, gpu-queue 220 -> 52. great quick triage everyone.
